rules.says: An agent is a definition under agents/, written before its first run: its text starts with its origin (the gap it was born for and how it is measured), it states its tools, and its tools only read. An agent adds a check to the Founder's own reading, the whole prepush, the bootstrap referee and the rival, and stands in for none of them.
rules.expects: Every file of agents/ is such a definition. A file that is not, or an agent that needs a tool that writes or runs, refutes the rule: the rule is rewritten with the check that agent's output then needs before the agent runs.

rules.says: An agent is started only as brain:<name>, with the message tests/agent_run.py packet wrote and nothing else, so what it was given (the task, the scope, the lessons in force, its own memory) is in the packet, and each run has one row that names that message by its sha256.
rules.expects: In the session's log, every Agent or Task call is of a brain:<name> type and its prompt is the message of one run row of that agent written in this session, one row a call. A call with no row (a run under another type, a prompt written by hand, a run not recorded, a row of an earlier session, a call an agent made itself) refutes it, and so does a text sent to an agent with SendMessage.

rules.says: Each finding is read against the code by the Founder in the session of its run and takes a verdict: caught (a test red before the repair and green after, or the rival's or the referee's confirmation), false_alarm (refused, with the reason), or carried (true as read and not repaired by this push; it names the report or the ledger row that keeps it open). unjudged is a state of the session that ran the agent only.
rules.expects: No finding of a run of an earlier session is unjudged, whether the agent's definition is still under agents/ or was removed. One that is refutes it; it is closed by an amending row.

rules.says: What an agent missed is known only from the judge that comes after it. Each run is answered in a later session by an outcome row: the commit that was pushed, what the bootstrap referee and the rival said of it (accepted, rejected, or unknown when no verdict was given), where that was read, and for a rejection each reason with whether its defect was in the diff the run read. A defect that was in that diff and that the run did not report is a miss, and it names the lesson written from it, a lesson in force when the row is written: the lessons in force are given to every later run, so a class missed once is in the packets that follow while that lesson or one that replaces it stands.
rules.expects: Every run of an earlier session has an outcome row, and every miss that was in the run's diff names a lesson (the writer takes an outcome only for a run of an earlier session and only with lessons then in force). A run left without its answer, or a miss without a lesson, refutes it; it is closed by writing the row (python3 tests/agent_run.py record --agent <name> with a file that carries outcome_of).

rules.says: An agent is given its memory: the findings of its earlier runs that were refused, are carried or are not judged yet, so it does not spend a run on what is already known. A finding that says an earlier one again carries repeat_of.
rules.expects: Under the rules fewer than one finding in ten is a repeat (the under_rules fold of tests/agent_run.py measure). One in ten or more refutes it: the memory did not reach the agent or the agent did not use it, and which of the two is written with the redesign.

rules.says: An agent stays while it catches and can have saved what it cost: it is retired or redesigned when five sessions of its runs caught nothing, or when after five sessions its least cost (what its runs cost, a floor where only a floor is known) is more than one median session for each finding it caught (tohum/00e E692, condition 4; cost_over_gain of tests/agent_run.py measure), or when under the rules it raises more false alarms than it catches.
rules.expects: No agent with a run is retire_due (by nothing caught or by cost_over_gain) or has more false_alarm than caught under the rules. An agent that is refutes it: its definition is rewritten or removed in the push that sees it, with a decision row naming the runs.

rules.says: The rules are a design, and a design is kept only while the runs under it are better than the runs under the design before it (tohum/00e E697, condition 3). A design the runs refuted is closed in this file's designs with the rows that recorded it, and its runs become the next design's comparison. Better is read from what does not follow the size of a push: the share of defects the later judge found in a run's diff among those and the ones the run caught, and the share of findings that were caught.
rules.expects: After five sessions whose runs under the design in force have an accepted or rejected outcome, against the design before it the missed share (missed over caught plus missed, in the runs with such an outcome) is not higher, and either it is lower or the caught share of all findings is higher. Anything else refutes it: that is recorded, the design is closed in designs, and the rules are designed again. Caught findings a run and tokens per caught finding follow what a push holds and decide nothing (the first design was closed on them: rows f2081, f2083, f2094, f2108); the cost is the rule earns' and the repeats are the rule remembers'.
